artists.biography: Soul Asylum is an American alternative rock band that formed in Minneapolis, Minnesota in 1983. The band originally formed in 1981 under the name Loud Fast Rules, with the original line-up consisting of Dan Murphy, Dave Pirner, Karl Mueller and Pat Morley. The latter was replaced by Grant Young in 1984. The band recorded three albums with Twin/Tone Records and two with A&M Records to little commercial success. However, in 1992, they released the triple-platinum album Grave Dancers Union, featuring their Grammy Award-winning single "Runaway Train". The band played the Bill Clinton inauguration early the next year. They also scored a platinum record with the album Let Your Dim Light Shine three years later. In 1998 they recorded Candy from a Stranger. Mueller was diagnosed with cancer in 2004, causing the band to organize a benefit concert on his behalf. Mueller died a year later. In 2006 they released The Silver Lining. Their most recent effort is entitled Delayed Reaction, which was released on July 17, 2012.

perplexity.description:
Soul Asylum's Let Your Dim Light Shine is a 1995 rock album that solidified the band's presence in the alternative rock scene of the 1990s. Released by Columbia Records, the album features a blend of melodic guitar-driven rock, introspective lyrics, and accessible songwriting, characteristic of the band's signature style. Musically, it expands on the sound established in their breakthrough album Grave Dancers Union, with a mix of anthemic choruses, gritty riffs, and emotional depth, while also exploring more polished production and varied arrangements.

As the follow-up to their commercial peak, Let Your Dim Light Shine marked a pivotal moment in Soul Asylum's discography. It included the hit single "Misery," which became a staple on rock radio and helped the album achieve platinum status. While critics noted a shift toward a more mainstream sound compared to their earlier work, the album was generally well-received for its consistency and songcraft. Commercially, it performed strongly, further cementing Soul Asylum's reputation as one of the leading alternative rock acts of the era.
